observations: Brand 'SINGER' is printed on the top right of the machine head in photo 0.
A large circular dial on the right side of the machine head appears to be a manual speed or stitch selector.
The machine is mounted on a stand with a flat base.
The needle and presser foot are visible.
The machine shows significant surface wear and scuffs on the plastic casing.
A watermark 'POSTED ON JIJI DAVID ALFRED' is visible across the center of the image.

claims.evidence: The power cord is not visible in the photo.
The internal mechanism and light fixture are not visible.

claims.claim: Japanese made, the motor runs smooth. All accessories and the original manual, never serviced because nothing ever went wrong.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The machine may not power on or the motor may be seized.
risks.proof: A video showing the machine powered on and the needle moving through a stitch.

risks.risk: The internal light bulb may be burnt out or missing.
risks.proof: A photo of the internal light assembly.

risks.risk: The manual speed dial may be broken or the stitch selector may be faulty.
risks.proof: A video showing the machine being operated at different speeds and stitch types.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Video of the machine powered on and sewing through fabric.
Photo of the internal light bulb.
Photo of the model number plate, usually found on the side or back of the machine head.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
